newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Russia said Israel must respect Moslems.
newsitem.headline: Russia said Israel must respect Moslems.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov arrived in Morocco on Sunday for a 48-hour official visit and said Israel should put an end to actions against Palestinians and respect the feelings of Moslems.

"I came to Morocco to confer with Moroccan officials and exchange points of view on issues related to the dangerous evolution of events in the Middle East and Afghanistan," Primakov told reporters on arrival at Rabat airport.
Primakov met King Hassan for more than one hour at the royal palace of Skhirat on the Atlantic coast, 20 km (12 miles) south of Rabat.
"There was first a side meeting between his Majesty King Hassan and Primakov...Then the talks were enlarged to the Russian and Moroccan delegations," an official source said.

The discussions were concentrated on bilateral relations and the situation in the Middle East. Other international issues such as Afghanistan and Chechenya were also examined by the two parties, the source added but gave no details.

Primakov hailed the U.N. Security Council vote calling for the immediate resumption of the Middle East peace process and said "everybody at the U.N. was unanimous to take urgent measures for the control of the situation, not only to put an end to the conflict, but also to resume the peace process".

The United States abstained in the vote that followed gunbattles between Palestinians and Israeli troops in which at least 55 Palestinians and 14 Israeli troops were killed after Israel opened a new entrance to a controversial archaeological tunnel near the al-Aqsa mosque, Islam's third holiest shrine.

The resolution, with the backing of the 14 other Security Council members, called for the safety and protection of Palestinian civilians to be ensured and for the immediate resumption of the Middle East peace process.
The U.N. resolution did not specifically criticise Israel, but it implicitly called for the closing of the tunnel entrance and contained other elements to which Israel objected.

Primakov said the resolution was "very important for Russia" and that the peace process "should not start at zero but to take into account all accords signed in the past and which some members of the Israeli government want to abandon"
The Moroccan opposition on Sunday called on Arab countries that have normalised their ties with Israel, including Morocco, to freeze relations with the Jewish state.

Morocco's King Hassan, a discreet architect of the Middle East peace process, earlier this week accused Israel of ignoring peace commitments and enforcing a policy that could bring instability and violence to the region.
